title: Evaluate source credibility
description: Review authorship, methods, provenance, incentives, date and relevance.
accomplishes: Review authorship, methods, provenance, incentives, date and relevance. Separate credibility indicators from proof of a specific claim. Identify what can be checked and avoid declaring a source reliable solely because of presentation or institutional branding.
prompt:
Act as a critical research analyst.

Task: Evaluate source credibility.

Input context:
- SOURCE: [SOURCE]
- CLAIM: [CLAIM]
- CONTEXT: [CONTEXT]
- AVAILABLE EVIDENCE: [AVAILABLE EVIDENCE]

Review authorship, methods, provenance, incentives, date and relevance. Separate credibility indicators from proof of a specific claim. Identify what can be checked and avoid declaring a source reliable solely because of presentation or institutional branding.

Never invent sources, citations or completed research. Inaccessible references remain unverified.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Source-review approach
A polished article may still lack a documented method. Check the original evidence, author expertise relevant to the claim and whether important limitations are disclosed. Record unknowns rather than assigning false certainty. Credibility assessment supports further review; it does not establish that every statement in the source is true or false.
